rules.section_title: APB4 to TL-UL Bridge Design Specification
rules.quote: A write with any other PSTRB value, and any access with a misaligned address, completes with PSLVERR = 1 and no TL-UL request is issued (DEC-001, REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002).
rules.condition: A write has PSTRB other than 4'b1111, or any access has a misaligned address
rules.statement: No TL-UL request is issued for a write with unsupported PSTRB or for a misaligned access.

review.reason: Quote states no TL-UL request is issued for these cases; checkable on interface.

rules.quote: Each APB transfer becomes one TL-UL request, and the TL-UL response becomes the APB completion.
rules.statement: Each APB transfer must become exactly one TL-UL request, and the TL-UL response must become the APB completion.

review.reason: Quote states one-to-one mapping of APB transfer to TL-UL request and response to APB completion; testable by scenario. Actor 'system' is acceptable.

rules.quote: The design goals are low latency and clean timing: the TL-UL request is launched from flip-flops in the first APB access cycle (see "early launch" in section 5.3), every output that changes toward either bus comes directly from a flip-flop, there is one clock domain, and the APB-facing logic and the TL-UL-facing logic are in separate modules. Feature ID: FEAT-003; Feature: Early launch of the TL-UL request from flip-flops; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-001, REQ-PERF-001
rules.statement: The TL-UL request must be launched from flip-flops in the first APB access cycle (early launch).

review.reason: Quote states early launch from flip-flops in first APB access cycle; the actor is the bridge, not a slave generally. Checkable every cycle from interface signals (TL-UL a_valid asserted in first access cycle), so assertion is appropriate. Actor should be the bridge/system.

rules.quote: Excluded: partial writes (any PSTRB other than 4'b1111); byte or half-word accesses; TL-UL bursts and multiple outstanding requests; the TL-UL-to-APB direction; TL-UL bus integrity generation or checking; a response timeout (the SoC watchdog handles a device that never responds, DEC-003); address decoding or protection; clock-domain crossing; software-visible registers.
rules.statement: The bridge does not support partial writes (PSTRB other than 4'b1111), byte or half-word accesses, TL-UL bursts, or multiple outstanding requests.

review.reason: Exclusions list out-of-scope features; not supporting them is not a behavioural obligation, but the bridge should not issue bursts/multiple outstanding requests; actor should be the bridge. Quote says excluded, so MUST_NOT is plausible; the check is assertion for single outstanding request.

questions.question: Which internal signals can be observed by the testbench (FSM states, reg_a_valid)? Several rules refer to internal state.
questions.note: The spec names internal registers and FSM states but does not say which internal signals the testbench may observe (hierarchical access or probes). The designer must define the observable internal signal set.

decision.answer: Black-box only: tests and checkers observe the top-level ports and nothing inside the DUT (REQ-VER-001 binds the checkers to the ports). Rules about internal registers and FSM states (BR-5.3-02, BR-5.4-02, BR-5.4-04, BR-5.3-11) are verified through their port-visible effects: request on channel A in the first Access cycle, a_valid held and channel A stable until a_ready, PREADY one cycle, next Setup accepted in the cycle after PREADY. The internal state itself is not_observable_at_interface.

questions.question: How should an illegal parameter be reported at elaboration of the verification source set (error, fatal, or assertion), and which tool performs the check?
questions.note: The spec says an illegal value is reported at elaboration of the verification source set (TEST-014 elaboration check). It does not define the mechanism (error, fatal or assertion) or which tool performs the check. The designer must decide.

decision.answer: Out of scope of the simulation flow: the elaboration check of illegal parameters (REQ-PARAM-001, TEST-014) is a static job, one Verilator elaboration per illegal value with an elaboration-time $fatal in the verification source set. Mark these rules static_or_structural; do not check them in simulation.

questions.question: ASM-001 is still Open and says a transfer that starts with PENABLE=1 is never answered. Is that hang an accepted behavior to test, or must the bridge recover or flag an error?
questions.note: The spec says a transfer starting with PENABLE=1 is never answered, but ASM-001 and OI-002 are Open. It does not decide whether that hang is accepted behavior to test or whether the bridge must recover or flag an error. The designer must decide.

decision.answer: Accepted limitation, not a DUT obligation: a transfer that starts with PENABLE=1 breaks REF-001 (APB4 Setup phase first), so ASM-001 stands. The testbench requester never produces it; the bridge need not answer, recover or flag it. Only the reset recovery (REQ-RESET-002) is verified. CHK-style tests must not expect a response to such a transfer.

questions.question: What is the 'project-specific default value' for user signals generated by baseline sources? It must be defined before checking.
questions.note: The TL-UL document does not define the project-specific default value for user signals; it is left to the project, and the layout is still TBD-001. The designer must define it. The bridge itself drives a_user to zero.

decision.answer: For this DUT the project-specific default of the generated user bits is all zeros: o_tlul_a_user = '0 on every request (REQ-IF-005, DEC-004); the received d_user is ignored (DEC-006). Check a_user == 0 whenever a_valid is high.

questions.question: Is the one-request-per-cycle limit a restatement of single-beat A-channel transfers, and is it on valid or on handshake?
questions.note: The TL-UL text says only 'Only one request per cycle'. It does not say whether this restates single-beat transfers or whether it counts valid or the valid/ready handshake. The designer must clarify.

decision.answer: It is a property of the handshake: at most one A-channel request accepted (a_valid and a_ready) and at most one D-channel response accepted (d_valid and d_ready) per cycle, which a single-channel TL-UL port satisfies by construction. For this bridge the stronger REQ-FUNC-004 applies: at most one request outstanding. No separate check beyond REQ-FUNC-004.

answered_questions.question: Does a misaligned access with PSTRB=4'b1111 or a read with arbitrary PSTRB also give PSLVERR=1? Is PSTRB ignored for reads?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. A misaligned access gets PSLVERR=1 and no TL-UL request, even with PSTRB=4'b1111. A read ignores PSTRB, so any PSTRB value on a read is accepted.

answered_questions.question: When an error is returned, how many wait states does the PSLVERR response take, and is it timed relative to PSEL/PENABLE?
answered_questions.answer: A local error (bad PSTRB or misaligned address) takes 0 wait states. PREADY and PSLVERR come together in the first Access cycle, and PSLVERR is asserted only with PREADY. A TL-UL error response has the same latency as a normal transfer (3 Access cycles with a prompt device).

answered_questions.question: Does 'early launch' mean TL-UL a_valid is asserted in the very first APB access cycle (PENABLE=1) or in the setup cycle registered so it is visible at access? Exact cycle must be defined.
answered_questions.answer: The request is captured at the edge that ends the Setup cycle, straight into the channel A flops. o_tlul_a_valid is therefore a flop output that is high in the first Access cycle (A1, PENABLE=1), one cycle after Setup.

answered_questions.question: What is the exact error response behaviour (PSLVERR timing, whether a TL-UL request is suppressed) for unsupported PSTRB or misaligned address, given partial writes are excluded?
answered_questions.answer: No TL-UL request is issued. The transfer completes with PREADY=1 and PSLVERR=1 in the first Access cycle, 1 Access cycle in total, with PRDATA=0.

answered_questions.question: If a write has both PSTRB other than 4'b1111 and a misaligned PADDR, or if a read has PSTRB nonzero, how should the bridge respond? Does a rejected transfer issue any TL-UL request, and does PSLVERR use the same timing as a normal response?
answered_questions.answer: Any illegal condition makes w_legal false, so there is a local error with no TL-UL request, and the response is the same whether one or both conditions apply. No priority between errors is needed. PSLVERR has the same first-Access-cycle timing. A read with nonzero PSTRB is legal because PSTRB is ignored on reads.

answered_questions.question: What does 'misaligned' mean exactly (PADDR[1:0] != 0 for 32-bit words?), and does the check apply to reads and writes alike?
answered_questions.answer: Misaligned means PADDR[1:0] is not 2'b00. The check applies to reads and writes alike.

answered_questions.question: REQ-FUNC-001/REQ-FUNC-003 and REQ-IF-005: a_size is given as 2 and 2'b10, consistent. But REQ-IF-005 says a_param 3'b000 and a_user all zero while REQ-IF-002 says d_user unused. Confirm a_user width.
answered_questions.answer: The a_user width is the parameter PARA_A_USER_W (default 1, range 1 to 32), and the bits are always driven to zero. The layout depends on the integration project (TBD-001), but the bridge drives zero either way. d_user is a separate, unused input.

answered_questions.question: REQ-PERF-001 says 3-cycle Access (2 wait states) but REQ-PERF-002 says 2 cycles when the response arrives in the acceptance cycle. Confirm that a_ready may be sampled in the first cycle.
answered_questions.answer: Yes. a_valid is high in A1 and the request is accepted at the end of A1 when a_ready=1. A response in that same cycle is allowed and supported, which gives a 2-cycle Access phase.

answered_questions.question: REQ-PERF-004 gives 4, 3 and 2 cycle Setup-to-Setup intervals. Which cycle counts as the start and end of each interval, and what exactly counts as a prompt device versus a same-cycle response?
answered_questions.answer: The interval runs from one Setup cycle to the next. 4 cycles is S plus 3 Access cycles, 3 cycles is S plus 2 for a same-cycle response, and 2 cycles is S plus 1 for a local error. A prompt device accepts in A1 and responds in A2. A same-cycle response comes in the cycle in which the request is accepted. These are minimum intervals.

answered_questions.question: Section 8 is referenced for illegal PARA_ADDR_W values. What does the design do if one is configured (elaboration error, undefined behaviour, or silent clamp)? This decides whether illegal values can be tested at all.
answered_questions.answer: An illegal value is reported at elaboration of the verification source set and is never silently clamped.

answered_questions.question: Does 'the Access phase is extended' when the response is late mean o_apb_pready stays low and o_tlul_d_ready stays 1? A1/A2/A3 timing is not defined for a late response.
answered_questions.answer: Yes. A late response or a_ready held low extends the Access phase by the same number of cycles. o_apb_pready stays low until the response is loaded and the APB FSM reaches DONE. o_tlul_d_ready stays constant 1.

answered_questions.question: BR-6.2-01 and BR-6.2-02 say PADDR[1:0] must be 0 and PSTRB must be 4'b1111 on writes, but BR-6.3-11 and BR-6.3-13 define the bridge's PSLVERR behaviour for violations. Are these input constraints on the master, or only conditions the bridge handles? Should the assertions be disabled in the error-injection tests?
answered_questions.answer: They are conditions the bridge handles, not prohibitions on the master. The bridge rejects them with PSLVERR and no TL-UL request, and the APB Requester model deliberately drives illegal requests. The bit-must-be-0 notes mean the legal value for a successful transfer.

answered_questions.question: For locally detected errors (bad PSTRB or unaligned address), what value does PRDATA take when PREADY and PSLVERR are 1? BR-6.2-04 says PRDATA holds its last value, and only the TL-UL error cases state PRDATA=0.
answered_questions.answer: PRDATA is 0 for every error completion, including local errors. The 'holds its last value' text applies only when PREADY is not asserted.

answered_questions.question: For a TL-UL response in the same cycle as request acceptance, what is the exact timing of PREADY relative to the A-channel handshake? Does o_tlul_a_valid drop in that cycle? BR-6.2-06 holds the valid until a_ready.
answered_questions.answer: The response is loaded at the end of A1, so PREADY is 1 in A2 (2-cycle Access phase). o_tlul_a_valid is still high in A1, the acceptance cycle, and is cleared when the request is accepted, so it is low in A2.

answered_questions.question: o_tlul_d_ready is 0 in reset and 1 only after the first clock edge following reset release. How should a D response in that window be treated: discarded as an orphan or accepted?
answered_questions.answer: A response in that window is discarded as an orphan. The TL-UL FSM is IDLE, a response counts only in WAIT or in REQ with a_ready, and w_resp_hit also needs reg_d_ready. No request can be outstanding in the first cycle.

answered_questions.question: The Reset value row lists reg_a_rd, reg_a_addr and reg_a_data as reset to 0, and the rule says o_tlul_a_opcode = 3'b000. Is opcode derived from reg_a_rd, so that 000 (PutFullData) is the reset value? Please confirm the mapping.
answered_questions.answer: Yes. Opcode bit 2 comes from the reg_a_rd flop (1 = Get) and bits [1:0] are constant 0. reg_a_rd resets to 0, so the reset opcode is 3'b000.

answered_questions.question: Synchronous release is provided by the SoC reset controller. Should verification check the release timing, or assume it as an environment constraint?
answered_questions.answer: Synchronous release is provided by the SoC reset controller. It is an integration dependency, not behavior of the bridge, so it is an environment assumption.

answered_questions.question: The a_user layout depends on the integration project (TBD-001). Is the always-zero requirement final for all widths?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. a_user is always driven to zero (DEC-004). Only the width is a parameter, and the bridge drives zero whatever the layout in TBD-001.

answered_questions.question: Is PARA_SRC_ID range 0 to 2^PARA_SRC_W - 1 checked at elaboration, and what is the expected d_source behavior when a response carries a different source?
answered_questions.answer: PARA_SRC_ID must fit in PARA_SRC_W bits (range 0 to 2^PARA_SRC_W-1), and an illegal value is reported at elaboration. A response with d_source different from PARA_SRC_ID completes with PSLVERR=1 (and PRDATA=0).

answered_questions.question: BR-9-02 and BR-9-04: Is a non-word-aligned address a master-side prohibition or a slave-side error response? Should the bridge still issue a TL-UL request when PADDR[1:0]!=0, or suppress it while returning PSLVERR?
answered_questions.answer: It is a slave-side error response. With PADDR[1:0] not 00 the bridge suppresses the TL-UL request and returns PSLVERR with PREADY.

answered_questions.question: BR-9-09: How is the expected d_opcode determined when the request was an error/suppressed one, and does a d_error from the TL-UL side also yield PSLVERR?
answered_questions.answer: A suppressed request has no TL-UL request and no response to check. For accepted requests the expected d_opcode is 001 for a read and 000 for a write. A TL-UL d_error=1 yields PSLVERR=1.

answered_questions.question: BR-9-08: PSTRB is mentioned in BR-9-01, but a_mask is always 4'b1111. How are partial PSTRB writes handled (DEC-001)? Is PSTRB != 4'hF an error or ignored?
answered_questions.answer: A write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111 is an error. It gets PSLVERR=1 in the first Access cycle with no TL-UL request. It is not ignored, and a_mask is always 4'b1111.

answered_questions.question: Does the first Access cycle for an illegal request mean PREADY is asserted in the cycle right after Setup (consistent with reg_pready set at the Setup edge)? Is the APB Access phase (penable=1) one cycle for the illegal case?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. The response flops are loaded at the end of Setup, so PREADY=1 and PSLVERR=1 in the cycle right after Setup. That is a 1-cycle Access phase (PENABLE=1).

answered_questions.question: For a legal request, does the TL-UL FSM go to REQ at the Setup edge simultaneously with the APB FSM going to BUSY, and how does this relate to launch via w_req_launch?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. At the Setup edge of a legal request, w_req_launch makes the TL-UL FSM go to REQ and load the channel A flops, and the APB FSM go to BUSY.

answered_questions.question: For ERR-003/004/005, does PREADY assert in the same cycle as the TL-UL d_valid response is accepted, or one cycle later? The quotes say 'with PREADY' without timing.
answered_questions.answer: PREADY comes one cycle after the response is accepted. The response is checked and loaded into the response flops at the end of the response cycle (A2), and PREADY, PSLVERR and PRDATA are output in the next cycle (A3). The latency is the same as OP-001 and OP-002.

answered_questions.question: For ERR-006, what is the expected behavior if a response arrives after reset abandons the transfer?
answered_questions.answer: The transfer is abandoned and no APB completion is sent after reset release. A late response then finds no accepted request and is discarded as an orphan.

answered_questions.question: Is each access-phase length an exact value or only a maximum? The quotes say 'Target / limit'. Is the access phase counted from PSEL/PENABLE assertion?
answered_questions.answer: The lengths are exact hard requirements: 3 cycles, 2 cycles and 1 cycle for the stated conditions. The Access phase starts in the cycle after Setup (PSEL=1, PENABLE=1) and lasts until PREADY is high.

answered_questions.question: Is the minimum transfer interval an exact period or only a lower bound? How does it relate to the access-phase lengths? The 4, 3 and 2 cycle intervals seem to be the access phase plus one setup cycle, but this is not stated. Also, 'As above' leaves the condition unclear.
answered_questions.answer: They are minimum intervals, measured from Setup to Setup. 4 cycles is S plus the 3 Access cycles, 3 is S plus 2 for a same-cycle response, and 2 is S plus the 1 local-error Access cycle. The same intervals apply when PSEL stays high, with no idle cycle added by the bridge. The conditions are the stated ones: prompt device, same-cycle response, local error.

answered_questions.question: The rule text for BR-14.3-01 ends with a dangling 'WHEN lint' fragment. Is there a condition that was cut off? Also, does the waiver cover only the five listed unused inputs, or may other waivers exist?
answered_questions.answer: The spec sentence is complete and has no cut-off condition. The lint waiver covers the five unused inputs i_apb_pprot, i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink and i_tlul_d_user. The spec also says the RTL complies without local exceptions.

answered_questions.question: BR-14.1-05 repeats part of BR-14.1-04 and BR-14.1-03 but leaves out the FSM names and the reset requirement. Should verification treat it as a separate rule or as the union of those rules?
answered_questions.answer: The spec has one list of the coding-baseline items that matter most, covering one module per file, structural top, ANSI ports, naming, FSM names, PARA_ comments, length limits and async reset on every flop. Treat the rule as that full union.

answered_questions.question: BR-15.2-01: the 'listed outputs' are not enumerated in the quote; which outputs are reset to 0 and is d_ready the only exception?
answered_questions.answer: The reset outputs are o_tlul_a_valid, o_tlul_d_ready, o_apb_pready, o_apb_prdata, o_apb_pslverr, o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address and o_tlul_a_data, all 0. d_ready is not an exception in reset, since it is 0 there and becomes 1 after release. The constant tie-offs (a_param, a_size, a_mask, a_source, a_user) hold their constant values.

answered_questions.question: BR-15.3-12 / BR-15.3-02 / BR-15.3-05: channel A stability checks apply only while a_valid is 1, but constants such as a_size and a_mask may be undefined when a_valid is 0; should SVA-005 be qualified by a_valid?
answered_questions.answer: The constant fields are tie-offs that never change after reset, so they are defined even when a_valid is 0. Stability checks apply only while valid is high and ready is low, and the REF-005 checkers sample channel A only while a_valid is 1.

answered_questions.question: What exactly does 'idle state after reset' mean for the IP (which signals or state values), and is it already covered by the reset behaviour rules elsewhere in the spec?
answered_questions.answer: Idle after reset means both FSMs are in ENUM_ST_IDLE and the listed flops (reg_a_valid, reg_d_ready, reg_pready, reg_pslverr, reg_prdata, reg_a_rd, reg_a_addr, reg_a_data) are 0. That is the same state already given in the reset section.

answered_questions.question: How will scan eligibility be checked (lint or DFT tool flow), since simulation cannot verify it?
answered_questions.answer: Scan eligibility is checked statically with lint and a scan rule check (TEST-018), not by simulation.

answered_questions.question: Does the misaligned-address PSLVERR in DEC-001 apply to reads as well as writes? The quote only mentions 'every misaligned address'. Is PRDATA 0 on those errors?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. The misaligned-address rule covers reads and writes. The error response is PSLVERR=1 with PREADY, no TL-UL request, and PRDATA=0.

answered_questions.question: For 'o_tlul_d_ready is 1 from the first edge after release', is it first observed high after that edge (flop with D=1) or already high before it? Is it still 0 during that first cycle?
answered_questions.answer: o_tlul_d_ready is a flop that resets to 0 with D=1. It is 0 in reset and until the first clock edge after release, and it is high after that edge. It is not already high before that edge.

answered_questions.question: Hosts never use non-contiguous masks, yet devices may or may not error on them. Should the testbench ever drive non-contiguous masks, and what response is expected?
answered_questions.answer: Hosts in this project do not use non-contiguous masks, and devices may or may not support them and may assert d_error. For this bridge a_mask is always 4'b1111, so the testbench never needs to drive non-contiguous masks.

answered_questions.question: Are the illegal-request cases host obligations or device-checked errors? Is d_error mandatory for every violation or only for the listed checks?
answered_questions.answer: Devices raise d_error for the listed checked properties (wrong opcode, address/size/mask combinations, non-existent addresses). The remaining basic properties of the TL-UL spec are enforced at design time by assertions with no HW checker, and devices and hosts may add stricter checks. So d_error is mandated only for the listed checks.

answered_questions.question: a_size should be 2 for PutFullData but must not exceed 2 in general. Is a smaller size for PutFullData allowed?
answered_questions.answer: a_size should be 2 for a 32-bit PutFullData, but the bus spec allows it to be defined otherwise. Size above 2 is never allowed, and PutFullData must mark all active lanes in a_mask. This bridge always uses a_size=2.
